reason: Prioritize small, local changes in the active panel32 loop: pointer scheduling and loop control have low correctness risk and little added timed work. Software pipelining and guarded prefetches may help, but add scheduling or instruction overhead; neither has active-path measurements. Packing, microbuffering, and padding add timed work or restructure the loop, with uncertain benefit. Transpose fusion could remove full-panel traffic in principle, but a small tile cannot serve all 16 column panels without retaining the full transpose, repeating transpose work, or changing accumulator scheduling. Reject any version that repeats transpose work per panel; first show a design that preserves the K update order and actually reduces total movement. The direct-A fallback proposal does not affect the fixed n=512 path. All advice is unmeasured; previous noisy or losing results on other paths do not establish causes here.
